How Batteries Work

A battery stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy through an electrochemical reaction.

The anode is the negative electrode and the cathode is the positive electrode during discharge.

Lithium-ion cells typically operate around 3.7 volts nominal and are widely used in phones and laptops.
